content: Prepare a healthy nursery and transplant healthy seedlings at locally recommended age and spacing. Timing depends on ecosystem, variety and monsoon onset; confirm the current district calendar locally.
The ICAR advisory describes nursery raising, field preparation, timely transplanting and locally suitable varieties. Dates and quantities are region-specific.
keywords: paddy nursery field preparation transplant kharif

content: Use soil-test-based nutrient recommendations. Nitrogen and potassium schedules depend on duration, ecosystem and local recommendation; avoid applying fertilizer by guesswork.
keywords: paddy rice nutrient fertilizer soil test nitrogen potassium

content: Rice water needs vary by soil, season and crop stage. Monitor water around panicle initiation, booting, heading and flowering; avoid a single fixed schedule for every field.
Good puddling and land leveling support uniform water distribution. Keep drainage available to remove excess rainwater.
Use a locally recommended cotton variety and sow within the suitable regional window. Timely sowing, field sanitation and crop rotation can reduce early pest pressure.
keywords: cotton sowing season variety field preparation

content: Scout cotton regularly for sucking pests and bollworms. Use field observations, sticky traps or pheromone traps as monitoring aids and follow local threshold guidance.
keywords: cotton pest scouting whitefly bollworm traps

content: Cotton irrigation should be adjusted to soil type, rainfall and crop stage. Square formation and boll maturity are important stages; adapt irrigation to weather.
keywords: cotton irrigation square boll maturity soil rainfall

content: Remove alternate weed hosts and avoid excessive nitrogen that encourages lush growth and pest build-up. Monitor regularly and use local IPM advice.
keywords: cotton weeds nitrogen field sanitation whitefly

content: Use balanced fertilizer based on soil testing rather than applying extra nitrogen by guesswork. Needs depend on variety, soil fertility, irrigation and yield target.
keywords: cotton fertilizer nutrient soil testing nitrogen

content: Tomato performs best in well-drained loamy or sandy-loam soil with organic matter. Avoid waterlogged plots and use soil testing to identify constraints.
keywords: tomato soil sandy loam season sowing

content: Raise healthy seedlings in a well-drained nursery and transplant vigorous seedlings carefully. Exact age and spacing depend on variety and production system.
Adjust irrigation intervals to soil moisture, crop stage and weather. Avoid prolonged water stress and waterlogging; drip irrigation can help when properly designed.
Use preventive IPM: crop rotation, field sanitation, removal of affected plant parts and regular scouting. Identify the pest correctly before any control action.
Sample representative areas separately when field conditions differ; keep soil records over time and use laboratory results before fertilizer decisions.
Tomato prefers well-drained loamy or sandy-loam soil rich in organic matter; waterlogging is harmful.
Clay soils often retain ponded water longer; irrigation intervals should be adapted to field condition and crop stage.

The TNAU tomato advisory lists Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at 50 g per litre of water for serpentine leaf miner management. Confirm current local recommendations and product suitability with an agriculture officer.
